title: A list and its reversal have the same per-element counts
statement: For any element a and list l over Nat, the number of times a occurs in l equals the number of times a occurs in the reversal of l.

formal.statement: theorem List.count_reverse : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : List.{0} AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (List.count x0 x1) (List.count x0 (List.reverse AxNat x1))))

evidence.supports: List.count_reverse is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example list_theorem_inventory -- List.count_reverse 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : List.{0} AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (List.count x0 x1) (List.count x0 (List.reverse AxNat x1))))')" -ge 1

notes: Induction on l (a fixed). The nil case is Eq.refl (reverse nil is defeq nil). The cons case unfolds reverse (cons head tail) to append (reverse tail) (singleton head), applies List.count_append to split that count into a sum, and closes with the same beq-head-a case split (needed again because count a (cons head nil) is itself Bool.rec-shaped) plus the induction hypothesis.
